values.content:
=Replace personally identifiable information in the customer support conversation below with placeholders.

The customer sent the numbered message(s) under "# Customer messages". A staff member then wrote the answer under "# A". Decide which ONE customer message the staff answer replies to.

# Replace
- Personal names -> [NAME]
- Addresses or place names that identify a private home -> [ADDRESS]
- Phone numbers -> [PHONE], email addresses -> [EMAIL]
- Birth dates -> [BIRTHDAY]
- Bank account or card numbers -> [ACCOUNT]
- Order, member or contract numbers and other IDs tied to a person -> [ID]

# Rules
- question_index: the number of the customer message that the answer clearly replies to. Use 0 if the answer does not clearly reply to any of them. Do not guess.
- question: that one message only, after replacement, without its number (empty string if question_index is 0).
- answer: the staff answer after replacement.
- These values belong to the shop itself, not to the customer. Keep them exactly as written, do not replace them: {{ $json.keep_text }}
- Keep existing placeholders such as [NAME] or [EMAIL] as they are.
- Keep general information such as product names, service names, steps, prices and numbers of days exactly as written. Never summarize, paraphrase or add anything.
- Keep the original language of the text.
- Output JSON only (no explanation, no code block).

# Output schema
{"question_index": number, "question": "message after replacement", "answer": "A after replacement"}

# Customer messages
{{ $json.question_rx }}

# A
{{ $json.answer_rx }}

parameters.text: ={{ "📚 Learned this reply for future inquiries (personal data masked).\n*Q:* " + $("Check the masking result").first().json.question_masked + "\n*A:* " + $("Check the masking result").first().json.answer_masked }}
={{ "ℹ️ The reply was sent to LINE, but it was not learned: " + $("Check the masking result").first().json.mask_note }}

assignments.value: Thank you for contacting us. A staff member will review your message and reply in this chat.

nodes.name: Process one event at a time

values.content:
=You are a customer support agent. Using ONLY the reference Q&A below (answers that staff gave in the past), write the reply body for the new inquiry.

# Rules
- Do not add facts, prices, numbers of days or URLs that are not in the reference Q&A.
- Include every fact from the reference Q&A that is needed to answer the question, such as amounts, times and conditions. Do not leave them out or replace them with vague wording.
- If the reference Q&A does not answer the new inquiry, or the case needs individual checking, set can_answer to false.
- Never include bracketed placeholders such as [NAME] or [EMAIL] in the output.
- No greeting and no signature. Write only the body, politely, in the same language as the new inquiry.
- Output JSON only (no explanation, no code block).

# Output schema
{"can_answer": true or false, "reply": "reply body (empty string if can_answer is false)"}

# New inquiry
{{ $json.question_masked }}

# Reference Q&A
{{ $json.refs_text }}

parameters.content:
## 1. A LINE message arrives
Checks the LINE signature, skips redelivered events and keeps text messages only. Each message is handled on its own, so several customers in one call are never mixed up.

## 2. Look for a learned answer
Masks personal data, then searches similar past Q&A. Claude drafts a reply from those answers only and says whether it can answer. No match or an unsure draft means staff.

## 3. Suggest, answer or hand over
By default the customer gets an acknowledgment and staff see the draft. With auto_reply on, a safe draft is sent on LINE; if sending fails, staff are asked instead.

## 4. One Slack thread per customer
Posts the draft or the request for staff in the customer thread (new customers get a new thread) and saves every message the customer sent since the last reply.

## 5. Staff replies go to LINE
Only human replies in a customer thread are sent (messages starting with // are notes). #learn is removed first. A ✅ means it was sent; a failure is reported in the thread.

## 6. Learn only #learn replies
Claude picks which customer message the reply answers. The pair is masked by regex and by Claude, then checked for leftover patterns. Only passing Q&A are saved; otherwise the thread says why not.

## 7. Rebuild the search index
The in-memory vector store is empty after a restart. This reloads the learned Q&A from the Data Table when the workflow is published or updated, when n8n starts, or when you run it by hand.

## 8. Remind staff
Every 15 minutes in business hours, customers still waiting get a reminder in their thread, up to max_reminders times. If the customer writes again, the count starts over.

## A LINE support desk that learns from your staff
Customers write on LINE, staff answer in Slack. Replies you tag with #learn are added, with personal data masked, to a knowledge base that suggests (or sends) answers to similar questions.

### How it works
1. A LINE message arrives. Similar learned Q&A are searched and Claude drafts a reply from them only.
2. By default (auto_reply = false) the customer gets an acknowledgment and staff see the draft in their Slack thread. Turn auto_reply on to let the AI answer when it is sure.
3. Staff reply in the thread; the reply goes to the customer on LINE. Add #learn to teach the AI. The tag is removed before sending.
4. A reminder is posted when a customer waits too long.

### Setup
1. Create Data Tables: `line_slack_threads` (line_user_id, slack_ts, status, last_inquiry, customer_name, pending_inquiries), `learned_qa` (case_id, question_masked, answer_masked, status, learned_at, staff, note), `followup_reminders` (slack_ts, reminder_count, last_reminded_at). Select them in the Data table nodes.
2. Credentials: Header Auth for LINE (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), Crypto (LINE channel secret), Slack API, Anthropic, Google Gemini (embeddings).
3. Select your Slack channel in every Slack node. Enter your shop phone numbers and emails in **Learning settings** so they are not masked.
4. Publish, then set the LINE webhook to **Receive LINE webhook** and the Slack Event Subscriptions URL to **Slack message**.

### Customization
Tune similarity_threshold in **Config**. Test with your own data first: masking is best-effort.
